item.title: The Ripple Effect of Going for It
item.description: Can you learn to captain a yacht at 62 and turn it into a world-traveling lifestyle? Absolutely! Below, Sine Maria shares a first-hand account of her family’s latest charter with Dream Yacht in the Balearic Islands. Read on for an inspiring look at courage, partnership, and what happens when you say yes to a new adventure on the water. The Ripple Effect of Going for It On breaking into worlds you weren’t born into, and what happens when you actually do the thing. By: Good Life Designed and Sine Maria If there’s one thing I’ve learned from my mom, it’s that life has so much to offer and the limit of your world is only limited by your ability to keep expanding. In the middle of the pandemic, as part of our collective pause, she and I decided to go through the whole Good Life Designed program together again. It was through that process that she decided she wanted to be closer to nature, swim more, and learn how to sail. She didn’t grow up around sailing, knew it was costly and a bit of a boys club, but always admired the access it gave those who knew how. That hobby could take you anywhere in the world. The world of sailing requires a unique blend of resources, courage, technical education, practice, and willing crew members to go along for the ride and be there while you figure things out on your first trips alone. It thrives behind heavy yacht club doors that some are born with access into – but most don’t even know exist. The dream of being certified as a sailor has an even smaller niche- attracting those who thrive on the pressure to read and respond to the chaos of the elements at sea while holding the responsibility of passengers’ lives in their hands. Now that I have experienced the reward that comes with that kind of responsibility – I see the draw. Breaking Into a World You Weren’t Born Into I tried to look into data about women certified sailors but couldn’t find any credible data because no one seems to be particularly interested in that stat – however I can tell you there aren’t many. Sailing, just due to the nature of it, the time it requires, the unease that comes with the experience, especially as you’re getting your first solo trips under your belt, is enough to send anyone right over the edge. It’s heady, it’s overwhelming, it’s complicated, it’s technical, and it feels uncertain and dangerous before you’re skilled and experienced enough to feel truly comfortable and at ease on the water. When Pernille got the ping to learn to sail, the biggest question was how, as a 62-year-old woman, was she going to do it. She tried visiting yacht clubs but as someone who wasn’t interested in the social component and was really looking for the technical skills to captain her own ship, it didn’t feel like the best place to spend her time or money. The classes and day sail opportunities to get out on the water were nice, but if she really wanted to learn everything she needed to, she needed something different. She came across Nautilus Sailing, a week-long course in the Sea of Cortez that would teach you everything you need to know about sailing and cap off the week with a test that would certify you to sail on your own anywhere in the world. My dad at the time was in the most stressful period of his career, navigating his independent school and their 400 families through Covid. Using his coveted spring break to learn to navigate another set of uncharted territories felt not quite like the vacation he needed. But he took a leap of his own and joined her anyway. They spent a week disconnected from everything to focus on learning the thing that would later give them access to the life they live now – barely imaginable to them then. Heading out on what feel like once-in-a-lifetime week long sailing experiences all over the world with friends and family. In 6 years since becoming certified, have now completed their 15th sail and have endless shared albums to show for it. They’ve sailed all over, eight times in La Paz, Mexico, once i…

item.title: French Polynesia Cabin Cruise: The Floating Boutique Hotel for Effortless Island Hopping
item.description: Imagine waking up in a comfortable suite aboard a premium catamaran. You stretch out on crisp sheets and wonder what spectacular view is awaiting you today. Will it be the majestic twin peaks of Bora Bora or the white sand beaches and tropical jungles of Huahine? You step on deck and sniff the air: today’s port is actually the vanilla-scented shores of Taha’a. That’s what life is like aboard a French Polynesia cabin cruise. Every day, you get to go on a new adventure. At night, you rest and relax in the comfort of a spacious cabin aboard a shared catamaran charter. For many travelers, the freedom to visit multiple destinations rather than be confined to a single resort makes a cabin cruise a much better option than a typical holiday on land. What Is a French Polynesia Cabin Cruise? A French Polynesia catamaran cruise or cabin cruise is a travel option where you book a private cabin with its own attached bathroom on a catamaran. Instead of chartering an entire yacht yourself, you share the vessel with a small group of other travelers. How Cabin Cruises Work The catamaran operates much like a small-scale cruise ship but with a personalized touch. Your captain navigates the islands, and an onboard steward prepares your meals. This vacation style eliminates the stress of trip planning, sailing logistics, and meal preparation. And since vessels are shared among travelers, cabin cruises are more affordable than booking Tahiti yacht charters . Why It Feels Like a Floating Boutique Hotel Unlike massive cruise ships that carry thousands of passengers, a catamaran hosts between 8 and 12 guests. This creates an intimate atmosphere, similar to that of a small hotel, except you also get to experience different destinations and activities every day. In French Polynesia, our cabin cruises are offered on the Bali 5.4, Lagoon 620, and the Fountaine Pajot Ipanema 58, each accommodating 12 guests. Comfort and Convenience: What Is a Cabin Cruise Like Onboard? Life aboard a cabin charter is defined by relaxation and comfort. Your catamaran features decks, shaded outdoor dining areas, and a forward trampoline net. This net is a great spot to lounge as the islands glide by. No jostling for sunbathing space on crowded beaches or lining up to rent gear from stands along the shore. You can get all the sun you want on deck, and the cruise includes the use of water sports equipment. You can step directly off the yacht’s transom steps into the water, swim, snorkel, or kayak to your heart’s content. Island Hopping Without Repacking or Airport Transfers With 118 islands and atolls spread across an area as vast as Western Europe, French Polynesia island hopping is all about discovering the unique character of each destination. However, having your base camp be a hotel or resort limits your options. It also means you have to go through a drawn-out process of getting there before you can visit each different island. Traditional travelers must pack their suitcases, check out of their resorts, take a taxi to the airport, wait in security lines, and fly to the next island, only to repeat the check-in process. Meanwhile, on Tahiti cabin cruises , you unpack your bags once on arrival. While you relax on deck or sleep in your cabin, the catamaran moves you between Tahiti and other destinations like Huahine, Raiatea, Taha’a, and Bora Bora. A Tahiti cabin charter eliminates the need for regional flights and ferry schedules, saving you both travel stress and vacation time. Space, Food, Privacy, and Seasickness: Honest Answers Before booking a sailing trip, it is normal to have a few questions about how things work on a boat. Here is what daily life aboard your shared luxury catamaran looks like. Space: Yacht cabins are smaller than hotel rooms, but they’re just as well-appointed. item.title: Private Sailing, Made Simple: How Dream Yacht’s Easy Crewed Charters Work
item.description: Dream Yacht’s Easy Crewed Charter is a simplified private yacht charter designed for people with no sailing experience, making it one of the most accessible and cost-effective ways to enjoy a sailing vacation. What Is Included with a Dream Yacht Easy Crewed Charter When you book an Easy Crewed Charter, you get a private yacht just for your group with key elements included: Professional skipper to handle navigation and safety. Private yacht accommodation for your group (cabins with beds, linens, and towels included) Insurance for the yacht and passengers Fuel, water and consumables — basics needed for your sailing itinerary Snorkeling gear and a paddleboard for watersports fun Harbor and port fees in most destinations (except ports with unreasonable rates) A hostess/cook, and half board or full board (depending on destination) These inclusions make the Easy Crewed Charter an all-in-one vacation! You arrive at the base, hop aboard, and all sailing and logistical concerns are professionally handled for you. What’s Not Included in a Dream Yacht Easy Crewed Charter The charter does not include: Flights and airport transfers. Alcoholic beverages and meals ashore. Crew gratuities, travel insurance, shore excursions, or personal expenses. This transparency helps you plan your actual trip budget up front. Privacy & Value Benefits of an Easy Crewed Charter 1. Your Private Floating Experience Unlike big cruise ships or cabin-share options, an Easy Crewed Charter gives you sole use of the entire vessel for your group. Whether it’s family, friends, or a special occasion party. This means: No strangers onboard , just people you choose to travel with Tailored itinerary , planned with your skipper based on your interests and the weather Flexible daily pace , swim, snorkel, explore ashore, or just relax without rushing 2. Ease for Non-Sailors Since the skipper handles all sailing and safety, you can enjoy the trip without sailing knowledge which is ideal for first-timers and vacationers who want comfort and convenience. 3. Better Value Compared to Luxury Crewed Charters While luxury superyacht charters can cost tens of thousands per week, Dream Yacht’s Easy Crewed option tends to be far more cost-effective because it focuses on essential services with optional upgrades (no forced inclusions of high-end extras). Many travelers find this a smart balance between privacy, professional service, and budget. Especially for group vacations of 2-12 people. Dream Yacht’s Easy Crewed Charter Destinations Dream Yacht’s Easy Crewed product is available around the world with a broad range of sailing grounds suited to varied tastes and budgets. The Caribbean Antigua British Virgin Islands Grenada Guadeloupe Martinique St. Martin Bahamas : Abaco & Exumas These spots offer turquoise water, calm sailing conditions, and beautiful beaches ideal for snorkeling and island-hopping. The Mediterranean Croatia Greece Turkey France Montenegro Perfect for history, scenic coastal towns, and classic European seaside culture. The Exotic Seychelles (Indian Ocean) Tahiti & New Caledonia (South Pacific) Belize & La Paz (Americas) Thailand (Asia) These offer a more unique, remote sailing experience among coral reefs, peaceful lagoons, and dramatic island landscapes. Explore The World on a Dream Yacht Easy Crewed Vacation The Easy Crewed Charter is a practical, budget-friendly way to enjoy private sailing without needing any sailing skills. It bundles the essentials; yacht, skipper, basic amenities, and some watersports gear, while giving you the privacy and freedom of your own floating vacation home. Whether you choose a tropical Caribbean loop, a Mediterranean island hop, or an exotic Pacific adventure, you control the pace, places, and experiences, all with professional support and minimal stress. item.title: 10 Tips for more sustainable sailing vacations
item.description: As the world’s top sailing tourism company we’re making sailing vacation more accessible for everyone with more destinations than anyone else. That means that together, we have the potential to make a real difference for the environments that we sail. No matter where you choose to sail, chartering puts you in close contact with nature’s most fragile ecosystems. We each have an important role to play in sustainable sailing and ensuring the future of our oceans, seabeds and reefs. While on vacation, there are some small actions that can be taken to help reduce our impact – and prevent minor blunders that can be hazardous to the environment over time, particularly when repeated by thousands of visitors. From shopping locally to conserving water, it only takes a little bit of effort to make greener, cleaner choices while sailing. After all, the pristine natural beauty of the bays, reefs and beaches is what makes visiting and sailing in these destinations so special. Here are our top sustainable travel tips to give back to the planet on your next sailing journey. 10 Sustainable Travel Tips: How to master sustainable sailing 1. Harness wind power This tip may sound obvious, but one of the best ways to help the planet while sailing is to hoist the sails! And it’s this more eco-friendly way of sailing that lets you slow down and discover the beauty in the journey. Wind can get you almost anywhere you want to go, especially if you plan ahead by proactively tracking wind conditions. Plus, this tactic makes for a more authentic sailing experience. To help read the winds, download a few sailing apps to your phone before your departure. Navionics , PredictWind , and Windy are great options for planning custom routes based on anticipated winds. 2. Avoid unnecessary energy usage Using your sails as much as possible isn’t the only way to reduce your energy consumption. In addition to keeping your engine off while the sails are up, try your best to only run the generator when needed. One of the main areas to focus on is the air conditioner. By opening up the hatches to enjoy natural breezes, you’ll find yourself needing to power up the A/C less often! Boats can cool down quite quickly, so give this method a go before powering up the air. If you can manage, leave optional items like hair dryers and electric razors at home. 3. Never throw anything overboard The sea is not a garbage bin, so never discard anything into the water. It puts marine life at serious risk, especially with plastics! Even garbage that seems harmless (like food scraps) should stay on the boat until you can dispose of it safely. To avoid lingering odors, make it a habit to empty all trash bins every time you stop by a harbor or marina. In windy conditions, it’s also a good idea to secure loose items like inflatable floats, napkins and paper. Finally, sustainable sailing means picking up any trash or debris you see, even if it’s not yours. Going above and beyond to throw away floating trash is an easy way to give back to the planet! 4. Minimize plastic usage with reusables An easy way to keep rubbish from piling up or ending up in the sea is to bring reusable water bottles, plates, silverware, and bags. Provision your yacht with large gallon bottles rather than single use sizes. When packing for your holiday , ask each or your travel crew to bring their own insulated cup or bottle, which also makes it easy to keep track of which drink is yours! The goal is to avoid polluting the ocean with plastic, so if you do need to bring disposable items aboard, prioritize paper or biodegradable materials. Bonus points if your items can be recycled! 5. Always be careful with chemicals It should go without saying to only empty your holding tank in approved areas, but allow us to say it again. Holding tanks should never be emptied near beaches, swimming areas, or pockets of marine life! If you have to add fuel to your yacht, pay close attention to avoid spilling anything into the water.
